first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, making onboarding friction the most immediate shared bottleneck. I would verify the prior onboarding and promotional-pricing records because both directions are consequential: simplification could improve activation and qualified revenue, while pricing may defend SMB acquisition but risk margin and lead quality. Run a guarded onboarding test with activation, time-to-value, qualified conversion, retention proxies, and segment-level quality guardrails.

final.rationale: Run a standard, randomized onboarding-simplification experiment this week. The verified prior shows shorter onboarding increased completion, reduced time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, directly addressing the current completion and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Use activation, time-to-value, qualified conversion, and 30-day retention as primary outcomes, with segment-level quality guardrails. Do not pursue promotional pricing as the primary experiment: although it lifted qualified revenue short term, the verified cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention and failed to sustain through renewal.
